topic.title: Businesses: policies, schedules and specialists
topic.shortdesc: Your assistant and each business it works for: what the business is, how its work is done, its budget, schedules and approval policies, and its specialists, with live numbers. Edit them here.

image.alt: The Businesses page: the assistant's card at the top, then each business with its description, budget, schedules and specialists, each card with open, done, cost and approval counts.

body.p: Your assistant takes every task: your chats and Converse requests, schedules, and incoming email, Odoo, social and webhook messages. Each task is filed under the business it is about, so a DMS email or a chat starting dms: is a DMS task. On work you started it can use every business's accounts (Odoo, mail, parcels, calendar and reminders, the Brain) and every skill. On work from outside it uses only that business's, and everything it proposes waits for you.
The assistant's card at the top shows its open tasks, tasks done and cost over the last days, and approvals waiting, over every business. Below it, each business shows:

ul.li: its description, and a link to how it works (such as How Desktop Machine Shop works): a note in the Brain with what good looks like and what always needs you (refunds always need you, for example). The assistant reads it before working on that business. Edit it on the Brain page to change how the work is done;
its daily budget and its schedules, with those that are off marked so;
its specialists, if it has any.

body.p: The specialists are the Software Lead (Command Centre: changes the app's code and raises pull requests), the Video Producer and the Blog Writer (3dpandme). The assistant hands them only that kind of work, and they report back to it on the same task. You can also start a message with a specialist's name, such as video: …, blog: … or software: …. A specialist's Mission and tools shows what it is for, its autonomy notes, skills, tools, schedules, the names you can address it by and what it is measured on.
Choose a card's title to see its tasks in the Inbox. Whether an action runs or waits is decided by the business's policies.

Choose Edit. Changes apply to the next task, and each business keeps a history you can restore. Each business gets Add specialist, Policies and History, and the assistant has its own History. A pencil on each card edits the assistant or that specialist. Choose Done when finished.
A business's description, budget and own schedules are set in the code; its how-we-work note is edited in the Brain.
If a change saved in the app no longer fits a newer version of the code, the page warns you and the code's version runs until you save again or reset it.

dlentry.dd: The id is lower case with dashes and can't change later, because tasks keep it.
What it is for and how it should behave. Both go into the agent's instructions. The assistant sees the first sentence of each specialist's mission when deciding whom to hand work to.

Only these skills are in a specialist's workspace, and it can reach only these servers (Odoo, mail, calendar…). The assistant has every skill and, on work you started, every business's servers, whatever its card lists.
The actions it is expected to propose.
Extra chat names, comma separated, as in podcast: ….
Each fires a task for it on a cron schedule, such as 0 7 * * 1-5 for 07:00 on weekdays, with the prompt you give it. Schedules can be turned on and off.

body.p: Remove deletes a specialist. Its tasks stay and count as the assistant's.
For each action type of a business, choose Waits for approval, Runs, listed in the digest or Runs straight away. Anything not listed sets the rest. Promote an action type once you trust it.
body.note: Work that started with an email, webhook or other outside message always waits for approval, whatever is set here.

body.p: Every save is a version. Restore brings back an older one; Reset to code goes back to how the code defines that business, or the assistant. Neither loses anything: your changes stay in the history.
